_about: Hatua in Swahili. Each line is English (left) and its Swahili (right). The app, the website and the backend all read this one file; anything missing here shows in English. Words in curly brackets, like {name}, are filled in by Hatua and must stay as they are. FIRST DRAFT: to be reviewed by a fluent speaker before use with families. Lines to check first are listed in _review.

_review.Does {name} speak in sentences of 3 or m: Swahili joins words together (nataka = I want), so '3 words' counts differently. Check the example in the hint still shows 3 words.
_review.Does {name} use 'I', 'you', 'she' or 'he: Swahili has one word, yeye, for both she and he. Check this still asks the same thing.
_review.How often does {name} seem very sad or d: Check the word for depressed (aliyesononeka) is clear and not too clinical for caregivers.
_review.Does {name} babble, repeating sounds?: Check the word for babble (kubwabwaja) is familiar.
_review.Does {name} play 'give and take' with yo: Check 'nipe nikupe' is the usual name for this game.
_review.Lying on their tummy, can {name} lift th: Check kifudifudi (lying on the tummy) is the word most caregivers use.
_review.Your community health worker recommends: Kenya now says Community Health Promoter (CHP). Check which name families know.
